units.function: open on the problem growing more urgent, then name the task the team was given

features.clause_structure: two clauses joined by a comma
original_instantiations: sprawl problems called increasingly important
team tasked with modeling city growth

units.source_excerpt: The problems caused by rapid urban sprawl are becoming increasingly important in the past few decades. Our team was tasked with modeling smart growth of a city in the light of urban planning theory.
units.reusable_pattern: State the problem as becoming more pressing, then say the team was tasked with the modeling.
prohibited_generalizations: do not open an abstract with a quotation the body also uses

units.function: map the state into a cube and read the angle and the length separately

original_instantiations: growth state mapped to a vector
smaller angle means more sustainable

units.source_excerpt: A state of growth is mapped into a vector in this cube. And the vector of ideal smart growth is represented by diagonal of the cube. The smaller the angle is, the more sustainable the city is.
units.reusable_pattern: Put the state in a vector, the ideal on the diagonal, then gloss angle as direction and length as speed.
prohibited_generalizations: do not reuse the pancake image from another paper

units.function: fold angle and length into one index with a weight the policymaker sets

original_instantiations: angle and length folded into one index
added parameter weighs the two elements

units.source_excerpt: Therefore, we integrate angle and length into an Smart Growth Index(SGI) with an added parameter illustrating how policymakers weigh importance between these two elements.
units.reusable_pattern: Combine two competing readings into one index and let one parameter say which matters more.
prohibited_generalizations: do not call the weight a trade-off the model was designed to make

units.function: close by naming what the fitted model reveals and how it was checked

features.quantitative_role: two cities, a thirty year forecast
original_instantiations: most influential budget factors named
sensitivity and an f test vouch for it

units.source_excerpt: we shed light on the most influential factors in budget and developed a smart growth plan. Utilizing sensitivity analysis and F test, our model is testified to be reliable.
units.reusable_pattern: End the abstract on what the numbers reveal, then name the two checks that vouch for the model.
prohibited_generalizations: do not close with a claim the computation demonstrates

units.function: open the body with two borrowed voices before any claim of the team's own

original_instantiations: two outside voices open the section
each quote tied to a bbc piece

units.source_excerpt: Poor accessibility is the common denominator of urban sprawl. Dr Reid Ewing, the National Center for Smart Growth, quoted from a BBC article.
units.reusable_pattern: Borrow a sentence from a named person and a named outlet before stating the problem.
prohibited_generalizations: do not invent a quotation

units.function: give the problem a number and a date range before naming its harms

features.quantitative_role: two percentages and two population counts
original_instantiations: urban share rising from a third to two thirds
city dwellers multiplied since mid century

units.source_excerpt: In 1950, 30 percent of the world's population was urban, but by 2050, 66 percent of the world's population is projected to be urban.
units.reusable_pattern: Anchor the problem with one share then and one share later, then list the harms.
prohibited_generalizations: do not round the cited figures

units.function: trace the idea back to a named conference and a named set of principles

original_instantiations: a commission adopted principles in a named year
several principles now count as the movement

units.source_excerpt: With an attempt to solve these problems, the Local Government Commission adopted the original Ahwahnee Principles in 1991.
units.reusable_pattern: Name the body, the document and the year that started the movement.
prohibited_generalizations: do not summarize a movement without its founding document

units.function: set two definitions side by side and say which one is usable

original_instantiations: two definitions placed side by side
the three-part one called clearer and practical

units.source_excerpt: There are at least two definitions about smart growth. The three E's sustainability raised by the latter is clearer and more practical.
units.reusable_pattern: Offer two published definitions and judge one clearer and more practical.
prohibited_generalizations: do not pick a definition without saying why

units.function: restate each assigned task as a numbered item, then answer it in the same item

original_instantiations: each task echoed then answered

units.source_excerpt: These problems and our work can be restated as the following lists. According to the three E's requirement, we designed a three dimensional baseline cube model.
units.reusable_pattern: Number the assigned tasks and answer each one inside its own item.
reusable_elements: can be restated as the following lists
prohibited_generalizations: do not restate a task without the model that answers it

units.reusable_pattern: Record the printed wording, including the wrong word, rather than silently correcting it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not correct the author's spelling in the excerpt

units.function: state the assumption, name the source, then declare it reasonable

original_instantiations: data called reliable, source named

units.source_excerpt: We assume that the statistics we collected from the website are reliable and accurate. Thus, this assumption is reasonable.
units.reusable_pattern: End an assumption paragraph by judging the assumption reasonable.
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave an assumption without its closing verdict

units.function: restate a negative assumption in plainer words

original_instantiations: stability restated as no disasters
named events excluded one by one

units.source_excerpt: In other words, there are no destructive nature or human disasters in the selected two countries, such as great earthquake, war and diplomatic disruption.

units.function: support one assumption with both observed evidence and an earlier assumption

original_instantiations: plans of two periods called identical

units.source_excerpt: We found that the growth plans of the two periods are rather identical. Thus, it is reasonable to assume the growth status of the two cities is successive with that of the past decade.
units.reusable_pattern: Ground an assumption on what was found and on an assumption already made.
prohibited_generalizations: do not stack two unsupported assumptions

units.function: borrow one published sentence to license calling budget the main factor

original_instantiations: a cited author calls budget the primary tool

units.source_excerpt: According to N.V. Prosyanik et al., the city budget is the primary tool to regulate social and economic processes. Therefore, it is reasonable to assume that in our metric budget is the major factor.
units.reusable_pattern: Cite one sentence, then mark the assumption reasonable on the strength of it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not assert a factor is major without a citation

units.function: preview a section as first, then, after which, at last

features.clause_structure: to begin with, then, at last
original_instantiations: section order given up front
the last step builds the cube

units.source_excerpt: To begin with, we summarized the main parameters used in our model. At last, based on the SGI, EDI, SJI and EPI, we developed a three dimensional baseline cube model.
units.reusable_pattern: Open a model section by listing its moves from 'to begin with' to 'at last'.
prohibited_generalizations: do not preview steps the section never takes

units.function: define each term of a formula in the sentence right after it

original_instantiations: first term read as direction
second term read as growth rate

units.source_excerpt: where the first term of the numerator is the cosine function of the angle between the current growth vector and the ideal smart growth vector. This term represents whether the direction of current growth is close to smart growth or not.
units.reusable_pattern: After a formula, say what the first term represents and what the second represents.
reusable_elements: the second term of the numerator
prohibited_generalizations: do not leave a formula without a term by term gloss

units.function: give the reader a recommended range for the free parameter

original_instantiations: weight set above a threshold for fast growers
a lower range advised for developed ones

units.source_excerpt: If growth rate is more important than growth direction, the parameter can be set larger, but it is recommended that the value set between 0 and that threshold especially in developed countries.
units.reusable_pattern: State when to raise the parameter, then recommend a range for the usual case.
prohibited_generalizations: do not give a parameter with no suggested range

units.function: say a denominator exists only to put the result on a convenient scale

features.quantitative_role: a range from zero to one
original_instantiations: denominator exists to rescale

units.source_excerpt: The denominator of the equation on the right hand is utilized to normalize the SGI to a range of 0 to 1 for the convenience of defining the extent of smart growth.
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a normalizing term by the range it produces and the convenience of that range.
prohibited_generalizations: do not add a normalizing constant without saying why

units.function: name the published method, then say what was changed and why

original_instantiations: a published index taken as the base
one indicator added to improve accuracy

units.source_excerpt: Based on his work and the data available, we updated this method. Additionally, we added life expectancy to our model to improve the accuracy of prediction.
units.reusable_pattern: Credit the source method, name the one change, and give the reason for it.
prohibited_generalizations: do not claim a method without its source

units.function: tie each chosen factor back to the dimension it stands for

original_instantiations: each factor tied to one dimension
weights taken from the definition

units.source_excerpt: Gini coefficient represents the fairness of income distribution, employment rate represents the labor market access. According to the definition, the weights are given respectively.
units.reusable_pattern: For each factor say which dimension it represents, then cite the weights.
prohibited_generalizations: do not weight factors without naming their source

units.function: state the decision rule as only when, otherwise

original_instantiations: all three must be positive
anything else counts as not smart

units.source_excerpt: It is only when all three values of the parameters are high that a city can achieve ideal growth. When all three parameters are positive, the growth is classified as smart growth. Otherwise it is classified as non-smart growth.

original_instantiations: the lowest of three decides the type
the index measures the level

prohibited_generalizations: do not summarize a model with a new claim

units.function: justify each constraint by the real thing it stops

features.clause_structure: to solve, we estimate, we can achieve

the estimate then dropped into the model

units.function: say requirements were turned into dimensionless indexes
